newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-ZUBI FACES OLD TEAM MATES AND PRETENDER BAIA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ZUBI FACES OLD TEAM MATES AND PRETENDER BAIA.

text.p: Valencia goalkeeper Andoni Zubizarreta will start Sunday's Spanish league clash with Barcelona well aware that it may be his last appearance against his old team mates.

Zubizarreta holds appearance records in both the first division and the Spanish national side. But at 35 he knows that the time will soon come to make way for younger men -- such as his opposite number this weekend, Vitor Baia.
The man known to fans simply as 'Zubi' spent five years between the posts at Athletic Bilbao in his native Basque country and won two league titles before moving to Barcelona in 1986.
A splendid eight years later, during which he won four league titles and one European Cup, Zubi made what looks likely to be the last move of his career, down the Mediterranean coast to Valencia.
During that time he has been Spain's regular first-choice.
However, the occasional gaffes which marred Zubizarreta's early performances have become all too frequent in recent years.

Zubi gave the ball to Michael Laudrup and then was sent off for bringing down the Dane in a crucial World Cup qualifier, while his slowness allowed Roberto Baggio to score Italy's winner in the quarter-finals of US '94.
Zubi's problems in his last season at Barcelona, followed by those of successor Carlos Busquets, led fans to talk of a 'Camp Nou curse' upon goalkeepers.
The jinx seemed to have been cured when coach Bobby Robson spent 800 million pesetas ($5.56 million) bringing Baia with him from Porto.
Baia made a series of fine saves and won a place in the hearts of the Camp Nou crowd.
But then things started to go wrong again.
Baia was twice badly positioned as Oviedo fought back for a 2-2 draw in Barcelona and looked unsure of himself in the 2-0 defeat at Real Sociedad.
Disgruntled fans jeered Baia after he had let in three goals in the first half hour of the Spanish Cup tie with Atletico Madrid earlier this month.

Only a dramatic fightback which brought Barcelona a 5-4 win saved the Portuguese number one from greater blame. Other Barcelona players were quick to show Baia their support by embracing him at the end of the game.
Another saving factor for Baia was the memory of an astonishing first-minute mistake by Busquets in a Cup Winners' Cup game the previous week.
Both the board and the Barcelona coaching staff stand behind Baia who could yet enjoy the success of the grand old man of Spanish goalkeeping.
